# Ablations (Phase 2)

<!-- Generated by `python -m mathscribe.ablation_report`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Each run changes one setting of
[`configs/train/ablation_base.yaml`](../configs/train/ablation_base.yaml). The list of runs is
in [`configs/ablations.yaml`](../configs/ablations.yaml). All runs use the same rows, seeds and
schedule. The runs are compared on the val set only, never on the test sets.

Base model `unsloth/Qwen3.5-4B`, 4,000 train rows, 500 steps, batch 8, learning rate 0.0002, GPU Tesla T4. Val set `latex_ocr_val`, the first 500 rows (rows sha256 `ecc9b49c38c1c363`).

How to read the tables:

- `[low, high]` after a value is its 95% confidence interval (bootstrap, 2000 resamples).
- *Δ* is the value of the run minus the value of the base run, on the same rows (paired
  bootstrap). A `*` shows that the interval does not include 0 (significant at the 5% level).
- There are 5 comparisons for each metric. When there is no real difference, about 1
  comparison in 20 still gets a `*`. Treat one `*` alone as weak evidence.
- *eval_loss* is the lowest validation loss during training (200 val rows), from the
  checkpoint that became the adapter.
- *Train $* is the training time only, at the public price of the same GPU
  ([`configs/gpu_prices.yaml`](../configs/gpu_prices.yaml)). The runs used free GPUs, so this
  is not money spent. Each result JSON in [`results/`](results/) and each run file in
  [`runs/`](runs/) has the full values.

## Differences from the base run

- `abl_rslora` (rsLoRA): normalized match is 2.6 points lower than the base run [-4.8, -0.6].

† The run continued from a Hub checkpoint in a new session. The peak VRAM is from the last session only, so it can be lower than the real training peak. The time and the cost count all sessions.

- `abl_base`: the last session took 3 s of 3,322 s training time. The run file has no best checkpoint, so the adapter is the last checkpoint and eval_loss is `-`.
- `abl_rslora`: the last session took 3 s of 3,389 s training time. The run file has no best checkpoint, so the adapter is the last checkpoint and eval_loss is `-`.

## Runs that were skipped

These settings were tried and do not work. They are not in the tables above.

| Run | Setting | Override | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dora` | DoRA | `lora.use_dora=true` | Smoke test on Kaggle (2026-11-17, Tesla T4, Unsloth 2026.11.6, PEFT 0.21.2, Qwen3.5-4B, 16-bit float32, vision layers on): loss and grad_norm were nan from the first logged step, so the adapter output was only "!" tokens (0% match on 20 val rows). The same smoke test without DoRA trained normally (train_loss 0.56, eval_loss 0.117). |
